root_cause.text: The UV hub-info allocation path in `uv_system_init_hub()` used `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` directly as the NUMA node for `kzalloc_node()`, so a deconfigured socket mapped to `SOCK_EMPTY` (`0xffff`) triggered an invalid node allocation and panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check in `arch/x86/kernel/apic/x2apic_uv_x.c` to detect `nid == SOCK_EMPTY` and replace it with `NUMA_NO_NODE`, and the commit message states that “When a socket is deconfigured, it's mapped to SOCK_EMPTY (0xffff). This causes a panic while allocating UV hub info structures.”

This causes a panic while allocating UV hub info structures.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid allocating per-hub data with an invalid NUMA node by falling back to `NUMA_NO_NODE` for deconfigured sockets.
intent_record.what: The code that initializes `new_hub` was changed from a single ternary expression to an explicit `if/else` block. For `bid == 0`, it still assigns `&uv_hub_info_node0`. For nonzero `bid`, it now stores `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` in a local `nid`, checks whether `nid == SOCK_EMPTY`, and if so replaces it with `NUMA_NO_NODE` before calling `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, nid)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change alters the NUMA node used for allocating per-hub data when a blade maps to a deconfigured socket. Instead of passing `SOCK_EMPTY` directly into `kzalloc_node()`, the code now falls back to `NUMA_NO_NODE`, ensuring allocation uses a valid node value and avoiding allocation failure or misuse of an invalid node identifier.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid allocating per-hub data with an invalid NUMA node by falling back to `NUMA_NO_NODE` for deconfigured sockets.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause: it prevents uv_system_init_hub() from passing an invalid NUMA node derived from a deconfigured socket (SOCK_EMPTY) to kzalloc_node() by falling back to NUMA_NO_NODE.

candidates.rationale: This directly passes uv_blade_to_node(bid) as the NUMA node to kzalloc_node(). When bid maps to SOCK_EMPTY, the resulting invalid node can trigger an invalid allocation and panic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation directly uses uv_blade_to_node(bid) as the NUMA node. If bid maps to SOCK_EMPTY, it yields an invalid node value and can cause a bad kzalloc_node() allocation and panic.

x86/platform/uv: UV support for sub-NUMA clustering

Sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) invalidates previous assumptions of a 1:1
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8a50c58519271dd24ba760bb282875f6ad66ee71
Author: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Date:   Fri May 19 14:07:50 2023 -0500

    x86/platform/uv: UV support for sub-NUMA clustering
    
    Sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) invalidates previous assumptions of a 1:1
    relationship between blades, sockets, and nodes.  Fix these
    assumptions and build tables correctly when SNC is enabled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
    Signed-off-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this function body anymore. The old code allocated hub info per node with `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, nodeid);`, but this commit changes it to allocate per blade and then use the blade mapping: `new_hub = (bid == 0) ? &uv_hub_info_node0 : kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, uv_blade_to_node(bid));`. More importantly, the function no longer uses `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` to derive the node for the hub-info array entry in the problematic old way; instead it builds a blade table first and later maps nodes to blades with `__uv_hub_info_list[nodeid] = uv_hub_info_list_blade[uv_node_to_blade_id(nodeid)];`. That indicates the fix for the invalid-node allocation path is already present. Since the vulnerable statement is absent and the new handling avoids directly using a deconfigured socket mapping for node allocation, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
